# Verification plan: `irq_ctrl`

- Task: prj-fa45b8ae0a:dv-plan
- Serves requirement: req-5fc7831312, "Verify the existing interrupt controller RTL."
- Source specification: `interface_spec.md` (approved, sha256:fb13927a542a48345d42b3507423c39ded9baabfe56889102dd07ab255b18962)
- Intent: block_verification of existing RTL
- Status: draft plan. Nothing in this plan has been implemented or run yet.

## 1. Verification approach

- **Environment.** A self-checking testbench drives `src`, `we`, `addr` and `wdata`, and monitors `rdata`, `irq` and `irq_id`.
- **Reference model.** A cycle-accurate model is updated at each rising edge of `clk`. It holds:
  - `ENABLE`, `MODE` and `PENDING`;
  - the remembered previous level of each source.
- **Combinational outputs.** The expected `irq`, `irq_id` and `rdata` are computed combinationally from the model state and `addr`. They are compared at every cycle, not only after edges.
- **Assertions.** Concurrent assertions (SVA or equivalent) bound to the DUT check the properties marked "A-" below.
- **Stimulus.** Directed tests (marked "T-") cover each requirement explicitly. A constrained-random test (T-RAND) runs all of them against the model.
- **Coverage.** Functional coverage items are marked "C-".
- **Configurations.** Every test runs at N = 2, 8 (default), 31 and 32. N = 32 exercises the full register width and the case where no acknowledge number is out of range.

## 2. Requirement traceability matrix

| Requirement | Feature | Tests | Assertions / checks | Coverage |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [req:IRQ-PARAM] | Parameter N, unused bits | T-PARAM, all tests at N ∈ {2,8,31,32} | A-UNUSED-ZERO; model compare on rdata | C-N-CFG, C-UNUSED-WR |
| [req:IRQ-RESET] | Synchronous reset | T-RESET | A-RESET-CLR; model compare | C-RESET-STATE |
| [req:IRQ-REG-RW] | ENABLE/MODE write | T-REG-RW | Model compare on readback | C-REG-WR |
| [req:IRQ-READ] | Side-effect-free combinational read | T-READ | A-READ-NOSIDE, A-RDATA-COMB | C-ADDR-RD |
| [req:IRQ-LEVEL] | High-level detection | T-LEVEL | A-LEVEL-SET | C-DETECT |
| [req:IRQ-EDGE] | Rising-edge detection | T-EDGE | A-EDGE-SET, A-EDGE-HOLD | C-DETECT, C-EDGE-PATTERN |
| [req:IRQ-DETECT-DISABLED] | Detection independent of ENABLE | T-DETECT-DIS | A-LEVEL-SET / A-EDGE-SET (no enable term) | C-DETECT (enable=0 bins) |
| [req:IRQ-W1C] | PENDING write-1-to-clear | T-W1C | A-W1C-NOSET; model compare | C-W1C |
| [req:IRQ-ACK] | CLAIM write acknowledge | T-ACK | A-ACK-ONE; model compare | C-ACK-ID |
| [req:IRQ-SET-WINS] | Set beats clear in same cycle | T-SET-WINS | A-SET-WINS | C-SET-CLR-COLLIDE |
| [req:IRQ-MASK] | irq = OR(PENDING & ENABLE) | T-MASK | A-IRQ-MASK | C-IRQ-CAUSE |
| [req:IRQ-PRIORITY] | Lowest-number priority, irq_id = 0 when idle | T-PRIORITY | A-IRQ-ID | C-PRIO-ID, C-PRIO-MULTI |
| [req:IRQ-CLAIM] | CLAIM read format | T-CLAIM | A-CLAIM-FMT | C-CLAIM-RD |
| [req:IRQ-LATENCY] | Combinational irq/irq_id | T-LATENCY | A-IRQ-COMB, A-IRQ-ONE-CYCLE | C-LATENCY |

Every requirement tag in the approved spec appears in the matrix above at least once.

## 3. Tests

### T-PARAM — [req:IRQ-PARAM]
- At each N in {2, 8, 31, 32}, write all ones to `ENABLE`, `MODE` and `PENDING`, then read each back.
  - Bits N and up must read 0.
  - Bits N-1..0 of `ENABLE` and `MODE` must read 1.
- Drive `src` all ones so that `PENDING` sets for every source.
  - `PENDING` bits N and up must stay 0.
  - Writes to those bits must have no effect.
- At N = 32 no bit is unused. Check that all 32 bits are usable.

### T-RESET — [req:IRQ-RESET]
- Bring the registers to non-zero values and set some edge sources' remembered level high by holding their inputs high.
- Hold `rst_n` low for one or more edges, then check:
  - `ENABLE`, `MODE` and `PENDING` read 0;
  - `irq` is 0 and `irq_id` is 0.
- Configure a source as edge-triggered with its input held high, then release reset. Its remembered level was cleared, so it is expected to detect an edge at the first edge where the input is high after reset. This follows from the spec.
- Use reset pulses of one cycle and of several cycles.

### T-REG-RW — [req:IRQ-REG-RW]
- Write walking-ones, walking-zeros and random patterns to `ENABLE` (addr 0) and `MODE` (addr 1).
- After each write, read back both registers. Confirm that only the addressed register changed and that it holds `wdata[N-1:0]`.

### T-READ — [req:IRQ-READ]
- Read every address, including `CLAIM` and `PENDING`, repeatedly with `we = 0`, holding `addr` steady and toggling it.
- Check that no register changes, and in particular that `PENDING` is not cleared by a read of `CLAIM`.
- Change `addr` between clock edges and check that `rdata` follows within the same cycle, with no edge needed.

### T-LEVEL — [req:IRQ-LEVEL]
- With `MODE[i] = 0`, pulse `src[i]` high for one cycle. Check that `PENDING[i]` sets at that edge.
- Hold `src[i]` high and clear `PENDING[i]` repeatedly. Check that it sets again at every edge.

### T-EDGE — [req:IRQ-EDGE]
- With `MODE[i] = 1`:
  - drive the sequence 0→1 and check that `PENDING[i]` sets at the rising edge;
  - hold the input high for many cycles, clear `PENDING[i]`, and check that it stays clear (an input held high sets it once);
  - drive 1→0→1 and check that it sets again;
  - toggle the input every cycle.

### T-DETECT-DIS — [req:IRQ-DETECT-DISABLED]
- With `ENABLE[i] = 0`, repeat the T-LEVEL and T-EDGE stimulus.
- `PENDING[i]` must set while `irq` stays low.
- Then set `ENABLE[i]`. `irq` must rise without any new source activity.

### T-W1C — [req:IRQ-W1C]
- With several `PENDING` bits set and all sources low, write random masks to `PENDING`.
  - Bits written 1 must clear.
  - Bits written 0 must be unchanged.
- Write 1 to a bit that is currently 0. It must stay 0, because the write never sets a bit.

### T-ACK — [req:IRQ-ACK]
- With several `PENDING` bits set and all sources low, write each id 0..N-1 to `CLAIM`.
  - Only that bit may clear.
  - Upper `wdata` bits are randomised, because only bits 4..0 are the id.
- For N < 32, write ids N..31. Nothing may change.
- Acknowledge an id whose `PENDING` bit is 0. Nothing may change.

### T-SET-WINS — [req:IRQ-SET-WINS]
- Hold a high-level source's input high, then write 1 to its `PENDING` bit. The bit must remain set.
- Acknowledge the same source through `CLAIM`. The bit must remain set, and `irq` must stay high if the source is enabled.
- For an edge source, schedule the rising edge on the same cycle as the clearing write. The bit must remain set.

### T-MASK — [req:IRQ-MASK]
- Sweep combinations of `PENDING` and `ENABLE` for level and edge sources.
- `irq` must equal the OR over i of (`PENDING[i]` & `ENABLE[i]`) in every cycle.
- Include these cases:
  - pending but not enabled;
  - enabled but not pending;
  - enabling and disabling while pending.

### T-PRIORITY — [req:IRQ-PRIORITY]
- Set several sources pending and enabled at once, including source 0, source N-1 and random sets.
- `irq_id` must be the lowest index in (`PENDING` & `ENABLE`).
- Clear sources one at a time and check that `irq_id` moves to the next lowest.
- Check that `irq_id` = 0 whenever `irq` = 0.
- Check that a pending but disabled lower-numbered source does not win.

### T-CLAIM — [req:IRQ-CLAIM]
- Read `CLAIM` (addr 3) in idle and in active states, including `irq_id` = N-1 at N = 32 (id 31).
- `rdata[31]` must equal `irq`.
- `rdata[4:0]` must equal `irq_id`.
- `rdata[30:5]` must be 0.

### T-LATENCY — [req:IRQ-LATENCY]
- Check that `irq` and `irq_id` change in the same cycle as the register change that causes them, with no extra edge. Causes to test:
  - a detection edge;
  - writes to `ENABLE`;
  - a `PENDING` clear;
  - a `CLAIM` acknowledge.
- A single-cycle pulse on a level source with immediate clear must produce exactly one cycle of `irq`.

### T-RAND — all requirements
- Constrained-random traffic over `src`, `we`, `addr`, `wdata` and `rst_n`. Writes are biased toward `PENDING` and `CLAIM` collisions with detection.
- The reference model is compared every cycle at all N configurations.
- Coverage closure is measured on the items in section 5.

## 4. Assertions

- **A-UNUSED-ZERO:** `ENABLE`, `MODE` and `PENDING` bits ≥ N are always 0 as seen on `rdata` ([req:IRQ-PARAM]).
- **A-RESET-CLR:** if `!rst_n` at an edge, the next cycle has all registers 0 and `irq` = 0 ([req:IRQ-RESET]).
- **A-READ-NOSIDE:** if `!we` at an edge and there is no detection, `PENDING` is unchanged; `ENABLE` and `MODE` are unchanged whenever there is no write to them ([req:IRQ-READ]).
- **A-RDATA-COMB:** `rdata` equals the register selected by `addr` in every cycle ([req:IRQ-READ]).
- **A-LEVEL-SET:** if `!MODE[i]` and `src[i]` at an edge (in reset deasserted), then `PENDING[i]` is set afterwards ([req:IRQ-LEVEL], [req:IRQ-DETECT-DISABLED]).
- **A-EDGE-SET:** if `MODE[i]`, `src[i]` and the previous `src[i]` was 0, then `PENDING[i]` is set afterwards ([req:IRQ-EDGE], [req:IRQ-DETECT-DISABLED]).
- **A-EDGE-HOLD:** an edge source whose input is held high does not set `PENDING` again after a clear ([req:IRQ-EDGE]).
- **A-W1C-NOSET:** a `PENDING` write never sets a bit that would not otherwise be set by detection ([req:IRQ-W1C]).
- **A-ACK-ONE:** a `CLAIM` write changes at most `PENDING[wdata[4:0]]` and nothing for ids ≥ N ([req:IRQ-ACK]).
- **A-SET-WINS:** detection plus a clearing write in the same cycle leaves the bit set ([req:IRQ-SET-WINS]).
- **A-IRQ-MASK:** `irq` == |(`PENDING` & `ENABLE`) ([req:IRQ-MASK]).
- **A-IRQ-ID:** `irq_id` == the lowest set index of (`PENDING` & `ENABLE`), or 0 if none ([req:IRQ-PRIORITY]).
- **A-CLAIM-FMT:** if `addr` == 3, then `rdata` == {`irq`, 26'b0, `irq_id`} ([req:IRQ-CLAIM]).
- **A-IRQ-COMB / A-IRQ-ONE-CYCLE:** `irq` and `irq_id` match the current register state with no extra cycle of delay ([req:IRQ-LATENCY]).

## 5. Functional coverage

- **C-N-CFG:** each N in {2, 8, 31, 32} was run.
- **C-UNUSED-WR:** writes with nonzero bits ≥ N to each of addr 0, 1, 2 (N < 32).
- **C-RESET-STATE:** reset applied with non-zero registers, with an edge source held high, and for 1 and >1 cycles.
- **C-REG-WR:** each bit of `ENABLE` and `MODE` written 0 and 1.
- **C-ADDR-RD:** reads of each addr; addr changes between edges.
- **C-DETECT:** per source, cross of mode {level, edge} × enable {0, 1} × detected.
- **C-EDGE-PATTERN:** an edge source with an input pulse, a held-high input, and a toggling input.
- **C-W1C:** per bit, written 1 while set, written 1 while clear, written 0 while set.
- **C-ACK-ID:** each id 0..31 written to `CLAIM`, binned as in range or out of range (≥ N), and as pending or not pending.
- **C-SET-CLR-COLLIDE:** cross of detection-collides-with-clear × clear type {`PENDING` write, `CLAIM` write} × mode {level, edge}.
- **C-IRQ-CAUSE:** `irq` rises from each cause: detection while enabled, enabling while pending.
- **C-PRIO-ID:** `irq_id` takes each value 0..N-1.
- **C-PRIO-MULTI:** number of simultaneously active sources {1, 2, >2, all}, with a disabled lower-numbered source pending.
- **C-CLAIM-RD:** `CLAIM` read with `irq` = 0 and with `irq` = 1, for each `irq_id`.
- **C-LATENCY:** single-cycle `irq` pulse observed; `irq` falls on the same cycle as a clear.

## 6. Completion criteria

- Every test passes at every N configuration, with no assertion failures.
- 100% of the functional coverage bins in section 5 are hit, with any exclusion justified, such as out-of-range ids at N = 32.
- Code coverage on the existing RTL is reviewed, and any holes are explained or closed.
- Signoff requires recorded evidence and independent review, per P6 and P9.

## 7. Open questions for the spec owner

The following behaviour is not defined by the approved spec. It is excluded from pass/fail checking until the spec owner clarifies it:

1. Whether the remembered level of a source is updated while it is in high-level mode. This determines what happens when `MODE` switches to edge while the input is high.
2. Whether a register write in the same cycle as `rst_n` low has any effect. The spec implies that reset wins, but does not say so explicitly.
3. Whether `PENDING` detection occurs at an edge where `rst_n` is low.
